title: The same plan checker for the same consultant
question: Do some permit consultants get their plans to the same City reviewer far more often than the rota would send them there?
finding: A plain count finds 28 pairs where one City plan reviewer handled 35% or more of a permit consultant's permits at a technical review station. Holding the year and the kind of permit equal, and setting aside single projects filed in one batch, leaves 1: Lau (Nelson) Chi Chiu handled 31 of the 56 permits listing Bin Lei at building plan check, where about 3 would be expected. On the published records, repeat pairings between consultants and plan reviewers are almost wholly explained by timing and specialty.
how: From the City's routing records for building permits filed since 2015 that list a permit consultant or expediter. For each consultant and each named reviewer at a technical station, the number of the consultant's permits the reviewer handled, against the number expected if the consultant's permits were shared out like all other permits of the same kind (counter, full review, new building, sign) filed in the same year at that station. System accounts and processing desks are left out.
limits: Reviewers specialise (signs, restaurants, towers, one district), and a consultant who files one kind of job will meet the same specialist again and again; the same-year, same-kind comparison removes some of that but not all. Counter permits are checked by whoever is on the desk, and a consultant who comes on the same weekday meets the same person. Assignment is not misconduct. The Controller's 2021 review found that senior managers could hand specific plan reviews to specific employees and that some projects got 'improper expedited permitting'; this table shows where repeat pairings are concentrated, which is where that question can be asked.

columns.t: Of the consultant's permits at that station
